QuestionStmt.S: 'n' small spherical drops of same size which are charged to 'V' volt each coalesce to form a single big drop. The potential of the big drop is

Solution.S:
Let the radius of each small drop be $r$ and charge on each be $q$. The potential of each small drop is $V = \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r}$.

When $n$ drops coalesce, volume is conserved:

$$\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = n \times \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 \quad \Rightarrow \quad R = n^{1/3} r$$

Total charge on the big drop = $nq$.

Potential of the big drop:

$$V' = \frac{nq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 R} = \frac{nq}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 (n^{1/3} r)} = n^{2/3} \cdot \frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r} = n^{2/3} V$$

Thus the correct option is D: $n^{2/3} \cdot V$.
